title: Forest Pond Ecosystem Web
subtitle: How are living things connected in a small pond?
coreQuestion: How are plants, animals, mushrooms, sunlight, and water connected?
learningGoals: Recognize producers, consumers, decomposers, and environment in an ecosystem.
Understand living things are connected through food, energy, and material cycles.
Know decomposers help turn leaves and remains into soil nutrients.
misconceptions: An ecosystem is only a group of animals living together.
Food chains only mean who eats whom and do not include sunlight, water, or soil.

hero.title: Forest Pond Ecosystem Web
hero.lead: A small pond is not just animals and plants; it is a connected web of life.
hero.sceneExplanation: The main scene is a warm forest pond: sunlight reaches plants, and insects, frogs, birds, foxes, mushrooms, earthworms, water, and soil are connected with a few clear arrows.
hero.childPrompt: Start from the Sun and find one route connecting living things.
hero.parentPrompt: Focus on connection and cycles, not a complex food web.

classificationGroups.name: Producers
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Plants use sunlight, water, and air to grow.
classificationGroups.parentNote: For children: living things that make their own food.
classificationGroups.misconception: Plants are just background for animals.

classificationGroups.name: Consumers
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Animals need to eat plants or other animals for energy.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Do not dramatize predation; focus on energy transfer.

classificationGroups.name: Decomposers
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Mushrooms, earthworms, and tiny microbes help leaves return to soil.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Mushrooms are not plants, but can be introduced as decomposer partners.
classificationGroups.misconception: Decomposers are useless or only dirty.

classificationGroups.name: Environment
classificationGroups.childExplanation: Sunlight, water, air, and soil help living things live.
classificationGroups.misconception: An ecosystem includes only living things.

representativeObjects.name: Sunlight
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Sunlight gives plants energy to grow.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking sunlight is unrelated to ecosystems.

representativeObjects.name: Plant
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Plants use sunlight, water, and air to grow and provide food or shelter.

representativeObjects.name: Insect
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Some insects eat leaves or nectar and may be eaten by frogs or birds.

representativeObjects.name: Frog
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Frogs live near ponds and eat small insects.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking frogs are only about water.

representativeObjects.name: Bird
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Birds may eat seeds, fruit, or insects, and can help spread seeds.

representativeObjects.name: Fox
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The fox is a larger consumer near the pond.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Seeing foxes only as bad characters.

representativeObjects.name: Mushroom
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Mushrooms help break down leaves and dead wood.

representativeObjects.name: Earthworm
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Earthworms move through soil and help loosen it.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking earthworms are only dirty bugs.

representativeObjects.name: Water
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Pond water helps plants and animals live.

representativeObjects.name: Soil
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Soil supports roots and holds water and nutrients.

steps.childExplanation: Plants use sunlight, water, and air to grow.
Insects or other animals eat parts of plants.
Frogs, birds, and foxes can form food relationships.
Leaves and dead wood are slowly broken down by mushrooms, earthworms, and microbes.
Nutrients in soil help plants grow again.
steps.parentNote: Build a cycle, not just a line.

steps.childExplanation: Plants root in soil, and many small lives live there.
If water or plants decrease, many animals may be affected.

comparePairs.title: Food chain vs Ecosystem

a.name: Food chain
points: shows energy passing from one to another

comparePairs.childConclusion: A food chain is a line; an ecosystem is a web.

comparePairs.title: Producer vs Consumer
comparePairs.childConclusion: Plants and animals have different jobs in an ecosystem.

comparePairs.title: Decompose vs Disappear
comparePairs.childConclusion: Leaves do not vanish; decomposers help return them to the cycle.

clickTasks.title: Find: who are decomposer partners?
clickTasks.prompt: Find the partners that help leaves return to soil.
clickTasks.wrongHint: Decomposers often work near leaves, dead wood, and soil.
clickTasks.successCopy: Correct! Mushrooms and earthworms help decomposition.

clickTasks.title: Connect an ecosystem route from sunlight
clickTasks.prompt: Tap the energy and nutrient route in order.
clickTasks.wrongHint: First think: where do plants get energy to grow?

clickTasks.title: Does an ecosystem include only animals?

options.label: No, it includes plants, decomposers, and environment too

wrongHints.animals-only: Plants, mushrooms, water, and soil also matter.
wrongHints.plants-only: Animals, decomposers, and environmental conditions also matter.

clickTasks.successCopy: Right! Ecosystems include living things and environment.

speakTemplates: If _____ becomes less, _____ may also be affected.
parentTips: Do not make the ecosystem a complicated food web first; explain 5–6 objects clearly.
On a walk, ask the child to find producers, consumers, decomposers, and environmental conditions.
Stress that no life is useless; mushrooms, earthworms, and soil all matter.

intro: Plants, insects, frogs, birds, mushrooms, and soil near a pond are not separate worlds.
They form an invisible web of relationships.
keyFacts: Plants use sunlight to grow and become a food source for many lives.
Animals eat plants or other animals.
Decomposers such as mushrooms, microbes, and earthworms help turn leaves into nutrients.
Water, sunlight, air, and soil are also part of an ecosystem.
copy.explainPrompt: Can you start from sunlight and describe one connection route near the pond?

acceptanceCriteria: The child can tell basic differences among producers, consumers, and decomposers.
The child knows sunlight, water, and soil are environmental conditions.
The child can explain at least one ecosystem connection with arrows.
